content.text: {"prompt": "A square, purely nonrepresentational abstract painting in oil and cold wax that fills the entire canvas edge to edge, with no frame, border, wall, room, or gallery setting. The composition is a slow standoff between pressure and refusal. The left two thirds is a broad, cool field of deep indigo and blue-black, built from thin translucent glazes and then scraped back with a wide palette knife, so that pale bone-white and ash-grey show through in long, level, patient bands. Pushing in from the right edge is a dense, hot mass of cadmium orange and vermilion, laid on with fast, heavy, diagonal strokes of a loaded brush. The strokes are thick and ridged, with dragged bristle marks, and they surge toward the center in a crowd of insistent gestures. Where the hot and cool areas meet, they do not blend. The boundary is a ragged, vibrating seam of broken color, scumbled and dry-brushed, with fine scratched lines cut through the wet paint. Slightly off center, low and to the left, is one small region of stubborn, matte near-black. It is dense and absolutely still, and the orange stops short of it, so a pocket of untouched pale space surrounds it. This is the unresolved remainder, and it holds the tension of the whole picture. A few tiny, sharp flecks of acid green and a single thin vein of clear lemon yellow glint in the cool field like small flashes of clarity. The upper left drifts into open, thinly painted emptiness, with the weave of the canvas visible and soft pale washes. The lower right becomes thick, layered impasto, dark under-layers showing through cracks in the bright top layers. The rhythm moves from calm, long horizontal sweeps to short, agitated, overlapping marks. The mood is serious, honest, and unfinished, and the surface is tactile and heavily worked. Use only color, gesture, texture, layering, and contrast. Include no recognizable objects, figures, faces, bodies, scenes, landscapes, horizons, machines, diagrams, symbols, icons, letters, numbers, or text."}
